answer: Each identity must pass a radio-frequency fingerprint check: the tiny hardware flaws in its transmitter — phase noise and I/Q imbalance — form a signature no two radios share, like one raven's call picked out of a flock. A farm cloning a thousand agents from a single software radio leaves one fingerprint across the whole terrace of the spectrum, while each honest agent shows its own. The delta is the cost: every fake needs a real radio. Limit: signatures drift with heat and age, and checks need lab-grade receivers, so pair it with stake, not as a sole gate.
